title: "5 · Validation"
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(ggplot2); source("R/theme_dgxe.R"); source("R/show.R"); source("R/pipeline.R")
fit_lasso <- function(A, b, lambda = 0.01, iters = 2000, ...) {
  xi <- numeric(length(b))
  for (it in seq_len(iters)) { old <- xi
    for (j in seq_along(b)) { r <- b[j] - sum(A[j, -j] * xi[-j]); xi[j] <- sign(r) * max(abs(r) - lambda, 0) / A[j, j] }
    if (max(abs(xi - old)) < 1e-9) break }
  list(coef = xi, support = which(xi != 0))
}
```

## Simulation

The library depends on the weather only, so the solution is a cumulative sum:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("simulate")
```

## One held-out season

The model is fitted to all seasons except 1998 (shared support of 12 terms, plus genotype deviations) and used to predict 1998 from its weather. All 199 genotypes are shown.

```{r}
yv    <- match(1998, tr$years)
train <- setdiff(seq_along(tr$years), yv)
f     <- fit_years(gram, train, fit_ssr, k = 12)
y0    <- apply(tr$Y[, train, 1], 1, mean)
pred  <- simulate(f$xi, Theta[yv, , ], y0)
f$names[f$support]
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
rows <- lapply(seq_along(tr$genotypes), function(g) { n <- tr$nend[g, yv] + 1
  data.frame(genotype = g, das = 1:n + tr$das0 - 1, APSIM = tr$Y[g, yv, 1:n], Model = pred[1:n, g]) })
d <- do.call(rbind, rows)
d <- reshape(d, direction = "long", varying = c("APSIM", "Model"), v.names = "biomass", timevar = "source", times = c("APSIM", "Model"), idvar = c("genotype", "das"))
d$source <- factor(d$source, c("APSIM", "Model"))
ggplot(d, aes(das, biomass, group = genotype)) + geom_line(aes(colour = source), linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.3) + facet_wrap(~source) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(dgxe[c("grey", "blue")])) + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "biomass (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe()
```

## Leave-one-year-out cross-validation

The same procedure is repeated for each of the 31 seasons.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
show_fun("cv_blocked", "evaluate")
```

```{r}
system.time(cv <- cv_blocked(Theta, tr, gram, fit_ssr, k = 12))
round(evaluate(cv$pred, tr, fixed_day = 99), 3)       # index 99 = day 113 after sowing
```

Predicted against APSIM biomass at day 113, all genotype-season pairs:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-width: 4.2
d <- data.frame(obs = as.vector(tr$Y[, , 99]), pred = as.vector(cv$pred[, , 99]))
r <- sqrt(mean((d$obs - d$pred)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
ggplot(d, aes(obs, pred)) + geom_abline(colour = "#9CA3AF", linewidth = 0.4) + geom_point(colour = dgxe[["blue"]], size = 0.5, alpha = 0.2) +
  annotate("text", x = min(d$obs, na.rm = TRUE), y = max(d$pred, na.rm = TRUE), label = sprintf("RMSE %.2f t/ha", r), hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.4) +
  coord_equal() + labs(x = "APSIM biomass (t/ha)", y = "predicted biomass (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe()
```

## Baseline without weather

As a reference, each trajectory is predicted by the mean curve of the same genotype in the other seasons.

```{r}
base <- array(NA_real_, dim(tr$Y))
for (y in seq_along(tr$years)) base[, y, ] <- apply(tr$Y[, -y, , drop = FALSE], c(1, 3), mean, na.rm = TRUE)
for (g in 1:dim(base)[1]) for (y in 1:dim(base)[2]) {
  v <- base[g, y, ]; ok <- which(!is.nan(v)); v[is.nan(v)] <- v[max(ok)]      # hold the last mean after the last other season ends
  base[g, y, ] <- v; base[g, y, 1] <- tr$Y[g, y, 1]
}
round(evaluate(base, tr, fixed_day = 99), 3)
```

The error as a function of time:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
err <- function(P) sapply(2:dim(P)[3], function(d) { ok <- !is.na(tr$Y[, , d]); sqrt(mean((P[, , d][ok] - tr$Y[, , d][ok])^2)) })
nd <- dim(tr$Y)[3] - 1
d <- data.frame(das = rep(2:(nd + 1) + tr$das0 - 1, 2), rmse = c(err(cv$pred), err(base)),
                model = factor(rep(c("model", "no-weather baseline"), each = nd), c("model", "no-weather baseline")))
d <- d[d$das <= 15 + 140, ]
ggplot(d, aes(das, rmse, colour = model)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(dgxe[c("blue", "burgundy")])) +
  annotate("text", x = 40, y = 0.5, label = "model", colour = dgxe[["blue"]], size = 3.4, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 40, y = 0.2, label = "baseline", colour = dgxe[["burgundy"]], size = 3.4, hjust = 0) +
  labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "held-out RMSE (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe()
```

## Choice of fitting method

All methods share the signature `fit(A, b, ...)`, so they can be compared in one loop.

```{r}
methods <- list(OLS = list(fit_ols), ridge = list(fit_ridge, lambda = 0.01),
                SSR_8 = list(fit_ssr, k = 8), SSR_12 = list(fit_ssr, k = 12), lasso = list(fit_lasso, lambda = 2e-4))
res <- cached("swap_methods.rds", do.call(rbind, lapply(names(methods), function(nm) {
  m <- methods[[nm]]; cv <- do.call(cv_blocked, c(list(Theta, tr, gram, m[[1]]), m[-1]))
  data.frame(method = nm, t(round(evaluate(cv$pred, tr), 3))) })))
res <- rbind(res, data.frame(method = "baseline", t(round(evaluate(base, tr), 3))))
res
```

## Number of terms

With the 13-term library the sparse model has little room to reduce complexity. Adding products of drivers (`pairs = TRUE`, 37 terms) gives a larger dictionary:

```{r}
Theta2 <- make_library(drv, pairs = TRUE); gram2 <- gram_stats(Theta2, tr)
ks <- c(6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 30, 37)
rk <- cached("rmse_vs_k_pairs.rds", data.frame(k = ks, rmse = sapply(ks, function(k) evaluate(cv_blocked(Theta2, tr, gram2, fit_ssr, k = k)$pred, tr)[1])))
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 2.8
#| fig-width: 5
ols13 <- res$trajectory_rmse[res$method == "OLS"]
ggplot(rk, aes(k, rmse)) + geom_hline(yintercept = ols13, colour = dgxe[["burgundy"]], linewidth = 0.4, linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(colour = dgxe[["blue"]], linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(colour = dgxe[["blue"]], size = 2) +
  annotate("text", x = 37, y = ols13, label = "13-term library, OLS", vjust = -0.7, hjust = 1, colour = dgxe[["burgundy"]], size = 3.3) +
  labs(x = "number of terms (37-term library)", y = "held-out trajectory RMSE (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe()
```
